answer: Continuous physical distance attestation: each agent must relay a hardware-timestamped radio pulse at a fixed cadence, and the network checks that consecutive hops imply plausible travel time across the registered area, like a ripple spreading only so fast across a terrace of relays. An operator cannot place two identities closer than the speed-of-light bound allows, so each extra identity needs genuinely separate hardware and a real physical site, costing real land — even a tundra outpost — plus power and maintenance per node.
